selection_rule: Rank candidates before running. Evaluate the top ready candidate with spatial component holdout before any submission artifact may be promoted. A projection is never a score.

candidates.name: Fabric-rotation boundary under active strain
candidates.physical_signature: A narrow corridor with a strong multiscale change in the local double-angle fabric orientation of independently measured topography, magnetics, and gravity; it is retained only where a strain-gradient and conductivity-gradient corroborate the rotation.
candidates.why_off_catalogue: Mapped faults are preferentially surface-expressed lineaments. A buried or oblique transfer structure can rotate fabric across the corridor without producing a single obvious scarp, so it can be absent from a surface catalogue while still perturbing geophysical fields and deformation.
candidates.non_fault_mimic: Lithologic contacts, volcanic-flow margins, drainage divides, and processing seams can also rotate local texture.
candidates.difference_from_known_work: This tests orientation discontinuity/rotation, not the previously reported multi-physics orientation agreement, simple ridge/scarp response, drainage alignment, tip relay, ring, radon, or direct conductivity-boundary surface. It uses no distance-to-catalogue feature.
candidates.expected_holdout_improvement: medium (pre-registered qualitative rank; not a score projection)
candidates.implementation_cost: medium: six core bands and three Gaussian scales; no new external data
candidates.data_status: Core mirror bytes are locally SHA-256 verified; organizer provenance remains unverified because the official data tab is login-walled.

candidates.name: Strain-saddle / magnetic-phase boundary
candidates.physical_signature: Saddles in the shear–dilatation invariant field co-located with a persistent magnetic phase boundary; the saddle seeks a transfer zone rather than a high-amplitude anomaly.
candidates.why_off_catalogue: Faults that accommodate distributed strain or partition slip can be weakly expressed at the surface yet impose a geodetic strain transition and a basement magnetic boundary.
candidates.non_fault_mimic: InSAR/GPS interpolation artefacts, terrain-correlated strain bias, and igneous contacts.
candidates.difference_from_known_work: Uses a joint strain-invariant saddle and magnetic phase condition; it is not a scalar tilt/Euler/depth-cluster or ridge-thinning method.
candidates.expected_holdout_improvement: low-to-medium (pre-registered qualitative rank; not a score projection)
candidates.implementation_cost: low-to-medium: six core bands; no new external data

candidates.name: Cover-suppressed basement-conductivity boundary
candidates.physical_signature: A matched basement-depth, conductivity, and gravity edge deliberately anti-conditioned on a sharp DEM edge, to select an under-cover boundary rather than a visible scarp.
candidates.why_off_catalogue: The anti-scarp condition explicitly targets covered structures that cannot readily enter a map drawn from surface morphology.
candidates.non_fault_mimic: Basin-margin lithologic contacts, groundwater salinity boundaries, inversion artefacts, and sedimentary facies contacts.
candidates.difference_from_known_work: Differs from an unconstrained straight conductivity/depth lineament by requiring three-field concordance and suppressing topographic expression.
candidates.expected_holdout_improvement: low-to-medium; the visible-catalogue holdout may systematically under-measure this blind-fault hypothesis
candidates.implementation_cost: medium: five core bands; no new external data

candidates.name: Radiometric hydrothermal-alteration halo across a concealed edge
candidates.physical_signature: A radiometric ratio anomaly that straddles, rather than follows, a concealed conductivity/magnetic edge; the target is an alteration halo around an upflow conduit.
candidates.why_off_catalogue: Alteration can persist where a fault trace is buried or lacks a young scarp, providing an independent hydrothermal signal.
candidates.non_fault_mimic: Primary lithology, soil/regolith variation, survey-striping, and radiometric processing artefacts.
candidates.difference_from_known_work: The intended test is a ratio-halo/cross-edge geometry, not generic radiometric–scarp fusion.
candidates.expected_holdout_improvement: medium but unmeasured; not viable until acquisition is independently verified

candidates.name: Spring-chemistry corridor intersection
candidates.physical_signature: Collinear hot/warm spring chemistry anomalies whose corridor intersects a concealed geophysical boundary.
candidates.why_off_catalogue: Fluid discharge can reveal a permeable structure that has no map-visible trace.
candidates.non_fault_mimic: Regional aquifer flow, anthropogenic wells, sampling-density bias, and lithologic permeability contrasts.
candidates.difference_from_known_work: It requires a chemistry-alignment intersection rather than using spring proximity as a scalar prior; nevertheless it is deliberately de-ranked because earlier hydro-conduit/radon families make novelty uncertain.
